items.direction: Narrate this as a high-energy, feel-good gaming YouTube video explaining the new police and wanted system in the game GTA 6. The Narrator is EXCITED and HAPPY the whole time: a thrilled, grinning friend who has just learned how smart the new cops are and is bursting to tell you. A huge smile you can hear in every line, bright and upbeat, warm and natural like real excited conversation, never like reading a script. Wide, lively pitch movement; real amazement on every reveal; playful delighted laughter in the voice on the funny bits (they remember your shirt, it has four legs, don't shoot the dog). Punch the key words with energy. Short lines like 'Hollow.', 'Solid white.', 'Flashing white.', 'And red.' are crisp labels with a beat after them. Pace quick and bouncy, about 170 words per minute, short crisp pauses; never flat, calm, sleepy, monotone or documentary-serious, and never shouty or fake. Accent: native General American English, neutral American accent from first word to last. VOICE IDENTITY: the same person and the same high energy from the first line to the last. Say 'GTA 6' as the letters G, T, A then 'six', 'GTA 5' as G, T, A 'five', 'GTA 4' as G, T, A 'four'. Say 'K-9' as 'kay nine'. Say 'CCTV' as the letters C, C, T, V. Pronounce 'Leonida' as 'lee-oh-NEE-dah' and 'Lucia' as 'loo-SEE-ah'. Read ONLY the text provided, word for word: stop right after the final sentence and never add, invent or continue with any words of your own. The text is given one sentence group per line: read every line in order, do not skip any line.
lines: In GTA 5, you could rob a store, hide in an alley for a minute, and the police forgot you ever existed.
In GTA 6? They remember your shirt.
Your haircut. Your car. The gun in your hand. Even who you were with.
Rockstar has rebuilt the cops from the ground up, and honestly, it might be the biggest change in the whole game.
So here's the plan. I'm going to show you exactly how the new wanted system works, how the police hunt you, and the best ways to escape.
And stay to the end, because Rockstar gave the police something nobody saw coming. It has four legs.
Welcome to Five Star Intel. Let's go!
First, a quick rewind. In GTA 5, the wanted level was basically a timer.
Do something bad, the stars pop up, and the police instantly know where you are. No witness needed. Like magic.
To escape, you break their line of sight, stay out of those vision cones on the minimap, and wait.
It worked. But after thirteen years, we all know the trick. Duck into an alley, count to twenty, done.
Rule number one. No witness, no problem.
In GTA 6, the police only come if somebody actually reports the crime. A witness makes a call. An alarm goes off. Or a tracker on a stolen car gives you away.
Think about what that means. If nobody sees you, and no camera or alarm catches you, there is no wanted level at all.
And if someone does call it in, you get the first brand new thing. Hollow stars.
Hollow stars mean a crime has been reported, and police are on the way, but they have no idea who did it.
Leave before they arrive, and they just investigate an empty scene. You, my friend, are a ghost.
That's the first of four star states, and you need to know all four.
Hollow. Reported, but they don't know it's you.
Solid white. They've identified you, and they have eyes on you right now. This is the chase.
Flashing white. You've broken their line of sight, but they're right behind you, searching the last place they saw you.
And red. You've escaped the chase, but you're still inside what the game calls a Hot Area. More on that in a minute, because it changes everything.
Oh, and the stars go up to six again. GTA 5 stopped at five. The sixth star is back, for the first time since the GTA 4 days.

lines: Now the really clever part. Under the stars, there's a row of little red icons.
Each icon is one thing the police know about you. It's basically their notebook, right there on your screen.
A person icon. They know what you look like.
A clothing icon. They know what you're wearing.
A car icon. They know your vehicle.
A weapon icon. They saw what you were carrying.
A camera icon. You got caught on CCTV.
And two little people. They know Jason and Lucia were together.
Six icons. Six clues. And here's the fun part. You can erase them, one by one.
Clothes known? Change your outfit. Hit a clothing store, or, and I love this, grab a spare outfit from the trunk of your own car.
Face known? Get a haircut. Or plan ahead, and put on a mask before the crime even starts.
Car known? Dump it, swap it, or get it resprayed.
In one preview demo, the players switched cars, the car icon vanished, and a police cruiser drove straight past them. No idea.
Caught on camera? Get rid of the footage. In Rockstar's Extended Look, the crew even sets their getaway car on fire to destroy the evidence.
And if the police are looking for a couple? Split up. Send Jason one way and Lucia the other. Reports say that alone can knock a star off your wanted level.
Okay. Remember those red stars? Here's why they matter.
When you escape a chase in GTA 6, it is not over. The area where you did the crime becomes a Hot Area.
Police stay there, holding your description. Walk back in wearing the same clothes, driving the same car, and the chase starts all over again.
So you can't just circle the block anymore. You have to actually change something, or stay away until things cool down.
And at six stars? The Hot Area is the entire map. There is nowhere to cool off. All of Leonida is looking for you.
And it gets harder. In GTA 5, every cop was a blip on your minimap, with a nice little vision cone.
In GTA 6, those blips are gone. If you want to know where the police are, you have to look. With your eyes.
There is a Focus ability that highlights nearby officers, even through walls. But you have to choose to use it.
Rockstar even showed Jason crouching behind cover, slipping out of an officer's line of sight. This is a stealth game now.

lines: So can you just outrun them? Ha! Good luck.
Rockstar North's co-studio head, Rob Nelson, said that at three stars or higher, escaping in a normal car is nearly impossible.
You need a hypercar, or a fast motorcycle. Otherwise, you have to out-think them, not out-drive them.
And stealing a nice car isn't free either. Modern cars can have trackers. Steal the wrong one, and it reports itself.
And now, the one nobody saw coming. Dogs.
GTA 6 police have K-9 units. In the demo Rockstar showed to Edge magazine, Jason and Lucia crash their motorcycle, and run for it on foot.
The cops send in a German Shepherd. It catches Jason, and pins him to the ground. Chase over.
And the best detail? The Rockstar developers in the room were begging Rob Nelson. Please. Don't shoot the dog.
So you can't just sprint into an alley either. Something faster than you is coming.
One last system, and this one follows you for the whole game. The Criminal Profile.
The wanted level is about right now. The Criminal Profile is about what kind of criminal you are.
Play ruthless, hurt people who didn't need to be hurt, and the world notices. Witnesses call the police faster. Armed citizens fight back. Rival gangs attack on sight.
Play it smart, scare people instead of shooting them, and Leonida goes a little easier on you.
For the first time in GTA, how you commit a crime matters as much as whether you get caught.
Now, a few things Rockstar has not told us yet. We don't know exactly which crimes earn which star. And nobody knows what shows up at six stars.
We'll find out together on November nineteenth. And the moment we do, it'll be right here.
So. The police in GTA 5 forgot you in a minute. The police in GTA 6 know your face, your clothes, your car, your weapon, and your partner. And they brought a dog.
Tell me in the comments. What's the first thing you're doing when you get your hands on this game? Running from the cops? Or robbing something?
If this helped, subscribe to Five Star Intel. We're just getting started. See you in Leonida!
